output_text: {"action":"answer","expression":"","queries":[],"pages":[244,214],"status":"answered","answer":"The Spotlight argues that treating personal data as property could worsen inequality because poorer and more vulnerable people may be induced to sell data that contains their digital identity, deepening existing inequities. Ownership also does not itself resolve unequal power or give people lasting control: data could be traded away, and property-based sharing may add transaction costs. A rights-based approach instead gives individuals fundamental, immutable rights that cannot be bargained away like property.
